plan: Represent the adapted recipe as freshly built dicts so neither adapt nor print_original ever mutates its inputs; print_original returns authored_text unchanged.
Compute one Fraction scale ratio (target_yield / recipe yield) and apply it to every ingredient quantity, including ingredients introduced by catalog results.
Rank catalog candidates for a name by (priority, catalog index) so lower priority wins and catalog order breaks ties deterministically.

Resolve each ingredient with a substitution loop guarded by a per-ingredient seen-name set: while the current name is excluded, apply the best candidate, mutate the working copy (quantity_factor, unit, preparation), and detect cycles when a name repeats.
Recursively resolve additional_ingredients from catalog results under the same exclusions and catalog, which yields chained adaptations and catches exclusions reintroduced later.
Accumulate equipment in a set (recipe equipment plus add_equipment minus remove_equipment), then audit it against available_equipment at the end; emit the adapted list sorted.
Collect wording_changes pairs from every applied choice and apply them as substring replacements over the authored instruction strings.
Accumulate reasons and warnings in sets and never return early, so every independently applicable impossibility reason is reported; output reasons and warnings sorted, choices in application order.

Include a __main__ acceptance block covering: 3→5 scaling, chained substitution, verb-and-equipment-changing substitution, reintroduced exclusion, multiple simultaneous reasons, byte-exact original printing after adaptation, and priority-based deterministic choice.
mechanisms: Fraction scale ratio applied uniformly to all quantities
substitution loop with per-ingredient seen-set cycle detection
recursive resolution of catalog-introduced additional ingredients
equipment accumulation set with final availability audit
wording-change pair accumulation applied to instruction strings
set-based reason/warning accumulation with no early return, sorted on output
authored_text passthrough for byte-exact original printing
